newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forex market inactive on lack of selling.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forex market inactive on lack of selling.

text.p: Trading in the Sri Lankan rupee was inactive on Wednesday morning as traders preferred to hold dollars, speculating on a depreciation of the local currency by the Central Bank, dealers said.
At 0515 GMT, the rupee was around 59.33 to the dollar after opening at 59.34. On Tuesday, the rupee closed at 59.36 near the Central Bank's selling rate, they said.
The Central Bank pushed the range down by a quarter of a local cent and fixed buying and selling at 58.1922 and 59.3678, respectively.
"No trading has taken place up to now because those with imports to cover can buy dollars from the Central Bank," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
"The Central Bank is very positive towards the dollar. No one is prepared to sell dollars right now, anticipating it to go up further," he said.
Overnight call money rates were at 9.5 percent after opening at the same levels.
